title: Un monstre de séduction  (A Monster of Seduction)

segments.t: At the agency, Andréa's ex-girlfriend Clémentine confronts her in the hall, right in front of Colette. Andréa has just denied being a serial seducer, so the timing could hardly be worse. Listen to their exchange in French first.
Clémentine! Qu'est-ce que tu fais ici?
Je dois faire ça pour guérir.
D'accord, mais une autre fois!
Tu es un monstre de séduction.
Clémentine, écoute.
Tu m'as dévorée comme une hyène!
C'est ridicule. Ça n'a pas duré un mois!
Je parle de sentiments! J'avais des sentiments pour toi.
Et tu as demandé à ton assistante de me quitter!
Non, c'est faux!
Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.
Je te pardonne.
Tu as besoin d'un nouveau médecin, tu es folle!
Les gens sont malades, non?
Oui? Allô?
Let's walk through it line by line. Andréa and Colette encounter Clémentine in the agency hall.
Clémentine! Qu'est-ce que tu fais ici?
'Clémentine! What are you doing here?' This long question phrase after Clémentine's name is the everyday spoken way to ask 'what'.
Je dois faire ça pour guérir.
'I have to do this in order to heal.' The first action word means 'must' or 'have to', and the linking word before 'heal' means 'in order to'.
D'accord, mais une autre fois!
'Okay, but another time!' The word meaning 'another' follows the feminine form of 'a'. Together with 'time', it means a different occasion, not one more repetition right now.
Tu es un monstre de séduction.
'You're a monster of seduction.' The word for 'monster' stays masculine even though Andréa is a woman. It is the name of the thing Clémentine compares her to.
Clémentine, écoute.
'Clémentine, listen.' Andréa gives a casual command for one person, dropping the word for 'you'.
Tu m'as dévorée comme une hyène!
'You devoured me like a hyena!' The past form has an extra feminine letter at the end because the object word before the auxiliary refers to Clémentine.
C'est ridicule. Ça n'a pas duré un mois!
'That's ridiculous. It didn't last a month!' The two-part negative wraps around the helper word in the past.
Je parle de sentiments! J'avais des sentiments pour toi.
'I'm talking about feelings! I had feelings for you.' The second verb is in the past form used for how things used to be.
Et tu as demandé à ton assistante de me quitter!

'And you asked your assistant to break up with me!' The request uses 'ask someone to do something'. French puts a short linking word before the second action, 'leave me'. Clémentine objects to having received the breakup message through someone else.
Non, c'est faux!
'No, that's not true!' Literally 'it is false', with Colette standing right there listening to every word.
Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.
'You're rotten! But it's over.' The first describing word has a feminine ending for Andréa. After 'it is', the form meaning 'finished' stays masculine; it refers to the whole situation.
Je te pardonne.
'I forgive you.' The little object word for 'you' sits right in front of the verb. Having delivered her big forgiveness line, Clémentine stalks away.
Tu as besoin d'un nouveau médecin, tu es folle!
'You need a new doctor, you're crazy!' Literally 'you have need of a new doctor', and the adjective at the end is the feminine form of 'crazy'.
Les gens sont malades, non?
'People are crazy, aren't they?' Literally 'people are sick, no?'. Andréa turns to Colette with an awkward smile, but Colette simply bids Ms Martel a polite goodbye and walks off.
Oui? Allô?
'Yes? Hello?' The second greeting is specifically for phone calls. A rising 'yes?' can also answer a ringing phone or ask the caller to continue. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
Clémentine! Qu'est-ce que tu fais ici?
Je dois faire ça pour guérir.
D'accord, mais une autre fois!
Tu es un monstre de séduction.
Clémentine, écoute.
Tu m'as dévorée comme une hyène!
C'est ridicule. Ça n'a pas duré un mois!
Je parle de sentiments! J'avais des sentiments pour toi.
Et tu as demandé à ton assistante de me quitter!
Non, c'est faux!
Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.
Je te pardonne.
Tu as besoin d'un nouveau médecin, tu es folle!
Les gens sont malades, non?
Oui? Allô?
So much for convincing Colette that she doesn't have a string of ex-girlfriends. Back at the agency, Audrey Fleurot is arriving for her meeting with Augustin. See you next time!
Merci, au revoir.
